Noncollision Facet Transition and Exact Outer-Envelope
Classiﬁcation in the Folded Tri-Octagon
A companion to Spherical Edge Extensions of the Folded Tri-Octagon: Exact Incidence Events, Natural Ter-
minations, and Convex Envelopes
Hilmir Frímann Halldórsson
Research manuscript v0.1 14 November 2026
Accepted mathematical investigation; manuscript and author review pending.
Project-internal research manuscript, not externally peer reviewed.
Abstract
The existing folded Tri-Octagon determines 21 supporting lines and 42 signed exits on a
concentric observer sphere. We study their explicitly declared convex envelope across the closed
interval from Crossing A to Crossing B. The accepted coincidence catalogue ﬁxes the endpoint
mergers but does not determine all intervening supporting faces. There is exactly one interior
change of the labelled maximal-face lattice: at midpoint-to-exit distance t = 3h, all 42 vertices
remain distinct while six symmetry-related face patches become maximal hexagons. The two open
chambers have 56 and 50 facets, and the transition has 44. Each aﬀected patch changes from two
triangles and a quadrilateral to one hexagon, then to two quadrilaterals. Exact supporting-plane
and polygon-side signs hold throughout each chamber; closure under true ridge adjacency proves
that no facet or interior combinatorial transition is omitted. The limiting polygons recover the
inherited A/B hulls. The complete closed-interval list has no ten-vertex maximal facet. These are
consequences of the ﬁxed exit family and convexiﬁcation convention, without selecting a physical
boundary, preferred observer radius, or dynamical law.
1 Question and contribution
Point coincidence and face reorganization are diﬀerent geometric events. Distinct exits can enter a
common supporting plane without meeting one another. The parent synthesis completely classiﬁes
ﬁnite line coincidences and the Original, A and B event hulls [ 2]. The present companion supplies
the intervening maximal-face classiﬁcation; it preserves those earlier results.

4 Exact certiﬁcates throughout each chamber
The accepted proof validates a ﬁnite facet list on each of (A, x∗), {x∗} and (x∗, B). Three numerical
hulls nominated candidates only. In the calculation chart, a proposed face with ﬁrst three points
a, b, c determines
N = (b − a) × (c − a), D = N ·a, r l = N ·pl − D. (9)
In this section pl denotes its charted coordinate tuple. Each component of N has degree at most two
in x; every residual has degree at most three. The accepted conditions are:
1. N ·N > 0 on the domain, so the proposed plane never degenerates.
2. Exactly the declared facet labels have zero residual. On an open chamber these are identically
zero polynomials; every other label has strictly negative residual throughout that chamber.
3. For every directed consecutive side (a, b) and each other face vertex c,
N ·((b − a) × (c − a)) > 0. (10)
The side polynomials have degree at most four. Their strict signs place every other face vertex inward
of each directed side. Consequently the proposed cycle is the genuine convex polygon boundary, rather
than a fan of rendering triangles. Complete zero sets merge all coplanar face pieces into their actual
maximal polygon. At x∗ the same tests are evaluated exactly at the algebraic parameter.

For a nonzero polynomial on an open chamber (l, u), the submitted method ﬁrst divides out every
exact factor x−l and x−u. Endpoint zeros are permitted and are treated separately at the exceptional
parameter. The remaining polynomial has no endpoint root. Its Sturm sequence is constructed by
diﬀerentiation and negative Euclidean remainders over K, using only positive remainder rescalings.
The diﬀerence in endpoint sign variations counts all distinct interior roots, including even-multiplicity
ones. Zero roots together with the required sign at the exact midpoint proves that sign throughout
the chamber. Persistent zero polynomials are handled separately; they are not isolated transition
candidates.
This gives uniform support, normal and side signs, not a ﬁnite-resolution sweep. The complete
residual polynomials and cycles are preserved electronically [ 3]. The 26 plane-orbit representatives
in Appendix A provide a compact exact description of every new-domain facet. No all-triples or
all-quadruples enumeration is needed for the completeness argument that follows.

5 Completeness and the closed-interval classiﬁcation
Lemma 2 (Closure under true ridge adjacency) . Let Q be a full-dimensional three-dimensional
convex polytope. A nonempty list of its actual maximal facets is complete if every true ridge of each
listed facet is incident with two distinct listed facets.
Proof. A ridge has exactly two incident facets. A small transverse planar section through an interior
point of the ridge is a convex angle; its two boundary sides correspond to those facets. Thus the
hypothesis includes both neighbors across every ridge of a listed facet: the list is closed under actual
adjacency.
The full facet-adjacency graph is connected. Radial projection from an interior point maps the
polytope boundary to a sphere. A path between two facet-interior points can avoid the ﬁnitely many
projected vertices and cross edge arcs transversely. Its successive facets give an adjacency path. If
a facet were omitted, a path from a listed facet to it would have a ﬁrst crossing from a listed to an
unlisted neighbor, contradicting closure.
Exact support, complete zero sets and strict cycles make every retained polygon an actual maximal
facet of H(x). Every certiﬁed polygon side is an edge of that facet and hence a true ridge of the
hull. The accepted incidence records contain two distinct listed facets at every such side. Lemma 2
applies at every parameter in each certiﬁed domain. Euler’s relation, connected vertex links and the
listed dual graph are consistency checks; they do not replace this argument.
Theorem 3(Accepted complete A–B classiﬁcation) . For the ﬁxed family ( 2), the labelled maximal-
face lattice is constant on each open interval (A, x∗) and (x∗, B). The complete closed-interval
partition is
{A}, (A, x∗), {x∗}, (x∗, B), {B}, (11)
with the counts and facet sizes in Table 3. Exactly one interior combinatorial transition occurs, at
x∗.

Proposition 4 (Accepted regrouping readout) . The group action gives six copies of this change.
Thirty-eight maximal facets retain their branch-label sets across the event. Twelve chamber edges
disappear at x∗ and six diﬀerent edges appear after it. The event edge set is exactly the intersection
of the two chamber edge sets.
These are direct consequences of the complete labelled lists [ 3, 4]. In the displayed patch, the disap-
pearing diagonals are (E05+, E17+) and (E09+, E16-); the new diagonal is (E10-, E21+). Persistence
of labels does not mean ﬁxed coordinates or ﬁxed metric shape. The envelope’s derived adjacencies
do not modify the 21 supporting lines.
6.1 Attachment to the inherited coincidence hulls
At A and B, all 42 branch labels map exactly to the inherited 18-point inventories. The accepted
correspondence matches coordinates, branch groups, full supporting zero sets, cycles and true edges
against those original endpoint records. It is not another enumeration of the historical 816 triples at
each endpoint.
Table 5: Images of the chamber facets at the inherited endpoints.

Source: Accepted limit maps and review, Section 3.5 [ 3, 4].
Each two-dimensional image in Table 5 has exactly the vertex set of its inherited target facet, and
every endpoint facet is covered once. The remaining chamber faces collapse to edges or points when
labels coincide. The reviewer checked full target vertex-set equality, not just containment [ 4, Section
3.5]. The individual maps remain in the incidence records.
At x∗, by contrast, all 56 faces from the ﬁrst chamber and all 50 from the second retain dimension
two. The aﬀected ones acquire a larger common maximal supporting zero set. This distinguishes
endpoint mergers from interior facet regrouping; neither matching counts nor a picture alone would
establish the correspondence.

7 Consequences and interpretation
Corollary 5 (Scoped facet-size exclusion) . No maximal supporting facet of H(x) has ten distinct
vertices for any A ≤ x ≤ B.
Proof. The complete closed-interval face list contains only triangles, quadrilaterals and hexagons,
including the inherited endpoint facets.
This is a consequence of the full classiﬁcation, not of D3h symmetry alone. It does not exclude
selected planar sections, subsets, projections, other enclosing families, or the independently oriented
decagonal-prism comparison. It supplies no universal prohibition on metric golden-ratio relationships.
The ﬁxed aﬃne exits and convexiﬁcation convention determine the chambers and incidences without
an added orientation or ﬁtted scale. Common positive scaling preserves them after normalization
by w. Reﬂecting the whole construction transfers the result to the other hand, with transformed
normals, correctly oriented cycles and retained material/edge labels.
The inherited three along-line distances are h, σh, σ2h, with σ = 1 +
√
2 [2, Corollary on the ﬁnite
three-term relation]. The support event at 3h is neither a fourth line coincidence nor an inﬁnite
recurrence. Sphere radii retain the additive w2/3 in ( 3). The golden ratio ϕ = (1 +
√
5)/2, original
close sphere and optional decagonal enclosure retain their separate roles.
Variation of x is static parameter comparison, not time, breathing motion, a moving-support law,
force, energy account or native trajectory. No preferred observer radius or material wall is adopted.
Original-to-A and beyond-B remain outside this paper.
8 Evidence layers and trusted computation
The original Windows investigation independently organized candidate generation and decisive check-
ing, but those programs shared its exact quadratic-ﬁeld arithmetic engine. The checker rebuilt the
folded geometry and recomputed the certiﬁcate predicates. Its recorded work includes 6,300 point
residuals, 972 side inequalities and 254 distinct monic sign forms; these are implementation counts,
not separate theorems [ 3].
The GPT scientiﬁc review ﬁrst replayed that checker in an isolated Linux copy with only the Conda-
name guard adapted. Stable result ﬁelds agreed. Six damaged certiﬁcates, an additional even-
multiplicity interior-root control and a positive endpoint-only-root control behaved as required. This
replay corroborates the shared engine; it is not another independent arithmetic implementation.
